name: allsorts-feature-ranges
instr:
Please add range-scoped features to shaping in `/app`, so callers can change typography over part of the input without shaping separate strings.

Add `allsorts::gsub::FeatureRange { pub feature: Feature, pub enabled: bool, pub start: usize, pub end: usize }`, deriving `Copy, Clone, Debug`, and `allsorts::gsub::Feature::KERN` with tag conversion support. Add `Font::shape_ranged(&mut self, glyphs: Vec<RawGlyph<()>>, script_tag: u32, opt_lang_tag: Option<u32>, feature_mask: FeatureMask, custom_features: &[FeatureInfo], ranges: &[FeatureRange], tuple: Option<Tuple<'_>>, kerning: bool) -> Result<Vec<Info>, (ShapingError, Vec<Info>)>`. Add `allsorts::gsub::apply_ranged(dotted_circle_index: u16, gsub_cache: &LayoutCache<GSUB>, opt_gdef_table: Option<&GDEFTable>, script_tag: u32, opt_lang_tag: Option<u32>, feature_mask: FeatureMask, custom_features: &[FeatureInfo], ranges: &[FeatureRange], tuple: Option<Tuple<'_>>, num_glyphs: u16, glyphs: &mut Vec<RawGlyph<()>>) -> Result<(), ShapingError>` as a free function.

Ranges are half-open indices into the original input glyph vector. Apply covering ranges in slice order, with the last setting winning over the supplied mask, custom features and implicit defaults. Maximal runs with identical effective feature settings form segments. No substitution may consume input from two segments, including nested contextual substitutions; backtrack and lookahead context can still see neighbouring segments.
